subject: Any way to deal with label switching in latent class modeling

messages.author: 0be29200f0a7e1a9
messages.subject: Any way to deal with label switching in latent class modeling
parts:
Dear all,

I am a new user to NIMBLE and I am trying to use nimble to fit latent class model. However, I don't know how to deal with the label-switching issue. I find the tutorial on Rstan, does anyone know the tutorial for NIMBLE?

Thanks a lot,
Jun

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Any way to deal with label switching in latent class modeling
parts:
Jun, thanks again for your question, and your use of nimble.

The exact approach to preventing label-switching might depend on your model itself.  However, if each latent class has a parameter specific to it, for example a group-specific mean parameter, then you can prevent label switching by imposing an ordering over the group-specific means.  For example, if you have 2 groups, with means mu[1] and mu[2], then you can impose the ordering mu[1] < mu[2] using the dconstraint distribution by including the following line in your model code:

code <- nimbleCode({
   ...
   one ~ dconstraint(mu[1] < mu[2])
})

then also supplying the value one = 1 in your "data" list argument to nimbleModel:

data <- list(...., one = 1)
model <- nimbleModel(code, ..., data = data)

There are certainly other more complex cases, but this sort of approach can usually be used to prevent label switching between groups.

I hope this gets you going, but feel free to be more specific with your model if a more specific answer would be helpful.

Cheers,
Daniel
